text:
cheng: Heads up — CI judge runs for onboarding/model-x-quant-pt2 are disagreeing vs local. CI says judge-A beats judge-B 58/42, my local runs are ~51/49. Not a tiny diff for a canary rollout.

sara: Ugh. saw one example earlier where the judge label flipped on re-run. Could be nondet in the runner or a subtle tokenization mismatch.

mike: Do we have the exact runner logs/artifacts? CI prints seeds but we recently changed the quant kernels on the A100 image — that can change floating rounding and affect judge models for close calls.

tara: CI environment: cuda: 12.2, pytorch-2.2-rocm? (we have a mixed fleet). Local dev box: cuda11+cpu fallback. I think the more likely axis is kernel precision + batching order.

ollie: Pasting an excerpt from the failing CI task log:```
CMD: ./eval_runner --seed 42 --batch-size 8 --judge judge-A --model model-x-quant.pt
[INFO] loading model, quant backend=v_llama_kernels
[WARN] non-deterministic kernel detected: flash_attention_v2 (tensor core heuristics)
[DEBUG] sample 123: judge_score: 0.512 vs 0.503
[DEBUG] sample 123 (re-eval): judge_score: 0.498 vs 0.501
```

eval-bot: CI summary: "judge_decision_variance": 0.11 across runs, "seeded_reruns": 3, artifact: s3://redwood-evals/1763504721/artifacts/decision_table.csv

sara: That variance number is too high for production decisions. We need to distinguish runner nondeterminism (we can fix) from model intrinsic close calls (we should handle in rubric).

mike: Proposed immediate steps: (1) add a deterministic post-process tie-breaker so CI decisions are reproducible, (2) add per-example judge delta reporting to dashboard, (3) run parity tests with quant backends pinned. Thoughts?

tara: For (1) I'd suggest deterministic tie-breaker: if |score_A - score_B| < 0.03, then use secondary heuristic (longer answer wins? lexical-based preference?) — but lexical heuristics can bias. Alternative: deterministic hash of model outputs + prefer lower hash. That is unbiased-ish and deterministic.

ollie: Hash tie-breaker is clean for automation but non-intuitive for humans debugging. Another option: fallback to smaller, high-precision judge model (judge-B-highprec) when margin < threshold. That keeps decision aligned to quality, but costs extra compute.

sara: Also we must add bias checks: if we introduce a deterministic hash tie-breaker, run the fairness battery to ensure it doesn't systematically favor a demographic or stylistic group. We should include per-subgroup flip rates in the report.

cheng: Good points. For CI wiring: add the following artifacts to the job: decision_table.csv (example-level scores + chosen label + tie-break reason), raw_outputs.tar (judge outputs), and env.txt (cuda/cuDNN versions). This should let us triage quickly.

mike: I'll update the runner to emit a deterministic "tie_reason" field: one of ["margin_decision","hash_tiebreak","secondary_judge"]. Also add a regression test that replays the artifact and verifies decisions are stable across three seeded runs.

ci-bot: note posted: job 12345 will now upload artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/1763504721/artifacts/; three-run stability required for green.

tara: Metric definitions note: we should stop using single aggregate win-rate for judge selection. Add: per-example flip-rate, margin-distribution (CDF), subgroup flip-rate, and calibration (P(win) vs empirical). Dashboard panel suggestions: histogram of margins, heatmap of flip-rate by prompt-category.

ollie: Also document quantization sensitivity: for model-onboarding create a small suite of 200 prompts where we run full-precision judge vs quantized judge across backends and compute per-example delta. If more than X% flip, flag for manual review.

sara: CI-level workaround (short term): mark any judge decision as "unstable" if margin < 0.03 and requires manual triage before rollout. Long term: runner fixes + tie-breaker strategy.

cheng: Action items I will own: 1) Add artifact schema + tie_reason field to runner (PR by EOD tomorrow). 2) Wire the three-run stability check into the CI job (mike). 3) Create dashboard panels for margin-distribution and subgroup flip-rate (tara). 4) Run the 200-prompt quant-sensitivity suite and post results (ollie). 5) Draft rubric doc for tie-breakers and bias checks (sara).

sara: I'll draft tie-breaker rubric, will include options and recommended defaults: prefer secondary high-precision judge for sensitive customers, hash-tiebreak for bulk automated runs, and require manual review for subgroup-sensitive prompts.

mike: I'll start a small experiment to reproduce nondet behavior locally by swapping kernel versions and forcing same seeds; will paste a reproducer here.

cheng: Thanks team. If anyone sees new flips, drop the artifact link here. We'll defer the canary until we have stability=green. :white_check_mark:
